presentation_summary: 40-year-old female was evaluated for decreased visual acuity and bilateral flashers and was diagnosed with bilateral panuveitis.
On questioning she reported a pruritic rash for 3 weeks on both lower extremities and a genital ulcer 6 weeks earlier that had resolved.
She otherwise felt well and denied arthralgias, oral ulcers, photosensitivity, chest pain, and shortness of breath.
She was sexually active with one male partner but was uncertain whether he was monogamous.
Exam showed copper-colored/hyperpigmented macules on both feet and ankles with overlying xerotic patches.
RPR was positive at 1:64, treponemal antibody was reactive, HIV screen was negative, and rash biopsy showed treponemal organisms.
Lumbar puncture showed 2 nucleated cells, protein 23 mg/dL, glucose 60 mg/dL, and nonreactive CSF VDRL.
Ophthalmology found an inferior retinal hole in the left eye and bilateral panuveitis.
She received 14 days of IV penicillin plus topical cyclopentolate and prednisolone, with complete resolution of rash and uveitis and no long-term visual acuity effects.
